title: Epiphanius: heretics boasted apostolic tradition — so Rome cannot tar us with their company
source_text: XXV. Epiphanius vero haeresi 33. speciatim idem docet de Ptolemaeo quodam haeretico, ubi verba ejus refert ex epistola ad Floram, cui pollicetur fore ut veritatem disceret eorum quae docebat, postquam dignata esset Apostolica traditione, quam, inquit, per successionem nos quoque accepimus. Haeresi autem 73. refert epistolam Semi-Arianorum in qua gloriantur se amplecti traditam a patribus fidem, & se velut haereditatem quandam servare eam fidem, quam ex Apostolicis temporibus, per patres, qui in medio diu usque ad eos fuerunt, susceperant. Non est ergo, quod Pontificii nostrum cum haereticis consensum nobis exprobrent in rejiciendis traditionibus, cum pessimi quique haeretici de quibusdam traditionibus non scriptis gloriati sint, & eo fuco sua perniciosa figmenta tegere voluerint, ut hodie Pontificii.
pass_a_gloss: But Epiphanius in heresy 33 specially teaches the same concerning a certain heretic Ptolemaeus, where he reports his words from the letter to Flora, to whom he promises that she will learn the truth of the things he taught after she has been counted worthy of the Apostolic tradition, which, he says, we also have received through succession. And in heresy 73 he reports a letter of the Semi-Arians in which they boast that they embrace the faith handed down by the fathers, and that they keep that faith as a kind of inheritance which they had received from Apostolic times through the fathers who were in the midst for a long time up to them. It is not therefore for the Pontificians to reproach us with consent with heretics in rejecting traditions, since the worst heretics have boasted of certain unwritten traditions, and have wished by that varnish to cover their pernicious figments, as the Pontificians do today.
pass_b_english: Epiphanius: Ptolemaeus sold 'apostolic tradition by succession' to Flora.
Semi-Arians likewise boasted a father-to-son faith inheritance from the Apostles.
Worst heretics waved unwritten tradition as cover — just as Rome does.
So they cannot brand our rejection of their traditions as heretic-company.

rejected: only Catholics ever appealed to succession
